RFC5305-2-1.note: Unchanged on re-read: TestISISTLVIPv4RoundTrip lost only its RFC1195-5.2-4 comment tag. Forbidden behaviour: rejecting a TLV that carries unknown sub-TLVs, or not skipping them so the next entry misparses. TestISISTLV22RoundTrip (tlv_core_test.go) keeps entry0's three uninterpreted sub-TLVs opaque and then asserts entry1's metric equals types.MaxMetric, which goes red on a wrong skip; TestISISTLVIPv4RoundTrip (with-subtlv) goes red if a type-1 sub-TLV is rejected. Negative TestISISTLV22Truncated proves an overrunning length is not skipped as absent.

RFC5305-3-1.note: Forbidden behaviour: a link advertised at 2^24-1 being walked by normal SPF. TestISISSPFMaxLinkMetricExcluded builds A-B at 16777215 and t.Errorf fires if B or C appears in the SPF result; the positive half proves 16777214 is still relaxed (B at 16777214, C at 16777224).

RFC5305-3-2.note: The quoted sentence governs a traffic engineering SPF implementation: "To preclude overflow within a traffic engineering Shortest Path First (SPF) implementation, all metrics greater than or equal to MAX_PATH_METRIC SHALL be considered to have a metric of MAX_PATH_METRIC." Ze has no TE SPF (RFC5305-3.7-1 is not-applicable for that reason). TestISISMetricWidth asserts clampMetric saturation in the normal SPF, a neighbouring rule (RFC5308-5-2 tags the same unit), so the tag proves a different obligation from the one the row states.

RFC5305-4-1.note: §4 excludes a prefix "advertised with a metric larger then MAX_PATH_METRIC". Forbidden behaviour: such a prefix being considered in normal SPF. The tagged negative in TestISISMetricWidth advertises exactly MAX_PATH_METRIC (0xFE000000), which §4 does not exclude by itself, and the route drops out because the path total with edge 10 exceeds the ceiling. No input advertises a metric larger than MAX_PATH_METRIC, so the unit proves the path-total ceiling rather than §4's advertised-metric rule.

RFC5305-4.1-1.note: spf TestISISLeakOriginationL1L2 now carries the row and drives the producer leakInto via LeakPrefixes. Clause 1 (bit set to 1 on a higher-to-lower advertisement): l2Derived enters the L2 graph with UpDown false and assertion 2 requires hasLeak(IntoL1, l2Derived, true), so a leakInto that did not set the bit on L2->L1 goes red. Clause 2 (a prefix with the bit set only goes down): alreadyDown carried in L1 with UpDown true must be absent from IntoL2 (assertion 3), isolated because l1Only from the same node, same graph, does leak up. Both recorded red on spf/leak.go leakInto. The remaining sentences are rationale. lsdb_wiring and redistribute tags stay as the originator-side half.

RFC5305-4.1-3.no_code_path: internal/plugins/isis/spf/leak.go LeakPrefixes builds IntoL1 only from the Level 2 result and IntoL2 only from the Level 1 result (leakInto with setDownBit true or false); no other producer re-advertises a prefix between areas at one level, so no same-level inter-area advertisement reaches TLV 135.
RFC5305-4.1-3.note: The condition, a prefix advertised from one area to another at the same level, never arises in Ze.
